added.scope_note: Study-qualified DCP-reactive PBS / 10 wt.% Indulin AT softwood kraft lignin formulation R10 (Ewurum and McDonald 2025); lignin percentage is relative to total polymer mass. The nominal DCP-containing formulation and source-reported reaction distinguish this R-series from the corresponding B-series simple blend. Table 1 reports a nonzero gel fraction of 4.7% for R10; this supports the source reaction distinction, not a certified final network or an extra selected property. Different lignin loadings distinguish the four candidates. Processing routes, specimens, translated labels and measured differences alone do not create additional identities. Composite denotes a lignin-filled polymer formulation, not a pure molecular species or a continuous-fiber laminate. The source says 0.25 wt.% DCP added to PBS. Its exact denominator and final retained DCP are not resolved; no final mass fractions, crosslink density, graft fraction, molecular architecture or chemical purity are inferred. Section 2.1 gives BioPBS FZ91PM/FZ91PB without resolving a single grade. Keep grade_id null; the R labels are study formulations, not commercial grades. Section 2.4 (PDF p.4) determines contextual gel fractions on hot-pressed DCP cross-linked PBS-lignin material, not the injection-molded tensile dog-bones. These results support formulation-level reaction context only and do not determine the tensile specimens’ gel fraction or final network. Independent catalog TGA context only,not independent experiment or production batch. Thermal-piece physical lineage/conditioning unknown. Source experimental reference only,not engineering limit. Onset criterion/DTGordinal/massbasis unknown;0±0 remains source literal,not zero-error certification or detection limit. R0/lignin/Tc/enthalpy/crystallinity excluded.

added.scope_note: Study-qualified DCP-reactive PBS / 20 wt.% Indulin AT softwood kraft lignin formulation R20 (Ewurum and McDonald 2025); lignin percentage is relative to total polymer mass. The nominal DCP-containing formulation and source-reported reaction distinguish this R-series from the corresponding B-series simple blend. Table 1 reports a nonzero gel fraction of 4.3% for R20; this supports the source reaction distinction, not a certified final network or an extra selected property. Different lignin loadings distinguish the four candidates. Processing routes, specimens, translated labels and measured differences alone do not create additional identities. Composite denotes a lignin-filled polymer formulation, not a pure molecular species or a continuous-fiber laminate. The source says 0.25 wt.% DCP added to PBS. Its exact denominator and final retained DCP are not resolved; no final mass fractions, crosslink density, graft fraction, molecular architecture or chemical purity are inferred. Section 2.1 gives BioPBS FZ91PM/FZ91PB without resolving a single grade. Keep grade_id null; the R labels are study formulations, not commercial grades. Section 2.4 (PDF p.4) determines contextual gel fractions on hot-pressed DCP cross-linked PBS-lignin material, not the injection-molded tensile dog-bones. These results support formulation-level reaction context only and do not determine the tensile specimens’ gel fraction or final network. Independent catalog TGA context only,not independent experiment or production batch. Thermal-piece physical lineage/conditioning unknown. Source experimental reference only,not engineering limit. Onset criterion/DTGordinal/massbasis unknown;0±0 remains source literal,not zero-error certification or detection limit. R0/lignin/Tc/enthalpy/crystallinity excluded.

added.scope_note: Study-qualified DCP-reactive PBS / 30 wt.% Indulin AT softwood kraft lignin formulation R30 (Ewurum and McDonald 2025); lignin percentage is relative to total polymer mass. The nominal DCP-containing formulation and source-reported reaction distinguish this R-series from the corresponding B-series simple blend. Its exact denominator and final retained DCP are not resolved; no final mass fractions, crosslink density, graft fraction, molecular architecture or chemical purity are inferred. Section 2.1 gives BioPBS FZ91PM/FZ91PB without resolving a single grade. Keep grade_id null; the R labels are study formulations, not commercial grades. Section 2.4 (PDF p.4) determines contextual gel fractions on hot-pressed DCP cross-linked PBS-lignin material, not the injection-molded tensile dog-bones. These results support formulation-level reaction context only and do not determine the tensile specimens’ gel fraction or final network. Independent catalog TGA context only,not independent experiment or production batch. Thermal-piece physical lineage/conditioning unknown. Source experimental reference only,not engineering limit. Onset criterion/DTGordinal/massbasis unknown;0±0 remains source literal,not zero-error certification or detection limit. R0/lignin/Tc/enthalpy/crystallinity excluded.

added.scope_note: Source-qualified solid formulation C with 10 phr recycled milled carbon fiber (mCF/rCF), PERBUNAN 3445 F NBR and the fixed Table 3 additives. The distinct 10 phr fiber loading defines the formulation relative to the other solid recipes and the existing mCF=0 REF. Identity is the source-defined solid NBR/recycled-milled-carbon-fiber formulation, not a specimen, test direction, curing condition, supplier grade or foam state. PERBUNAN 3445 in Table 2 abbreviates the section 2.1 PERBUNAN 3445 F input, not a second material. Sul is ACTMIX S-80 product input as added; no conversion to elemental sulfur or to a fully specified chemical composition is made. The recycled fiber input is not assumed to be pure carbon, and no source-unstated final mass fractions or filler-purity correction are inferred. Table 3 loadings are retained in phr without normalization. Selected Table4 C tensile fact;phr unchanged. n,participants,weights,gauge,conditioning andextraction/pooling order unknown. Not engineering allowable or automatic mechanics input.

added.basis_note: Source section3.3 pools tensile results across specimens/directions;reported mean,not paired raw curves or certified directional equivalence.

evidence.locator: Article §2.2, tensile-test and orientation paragraphs: ISO 37 Type 2 specimens and Zwick Z005 at 500 mm/min are specified, but the tensile test temperature is not stated. §2.3 mixing/press temperatures are processing conditions, not tensile test temperature.

temperature.notes: Tensile-test temperature is not stated. Mixing at 110 °C and pressing at 170 °C are preparation conditions, not testing temperatures; no standard laboratory default is assigned.

test_standard.notes: Source-stated method; edition and independent compliance verification are not supplied.

test_method.text: ISO 37 tensile testing with Type 2 dumbbell specimens cut from nominally 2 mm vulcanized sheets; Zwick Z005 universal testing machine with a 5 kN load cell, at 500 mm/min crosshead speed. Two mutually perpendicular specimen orientations were tested and the source averaged tensile results across all specimens regardless of orientation. Numerical gauge geometry, detailed stress/strength extraction convention, test temperature, humidity, conditioning and tensile specimen count are not established in the selected source statements.
test_method.notes: Source-labelled finite-elongation stress, not modulus slope; 5kN is instrument capacity. ISO2024 terminology reference does not identify the edition used by authors or prove compliance.

direction.text: Tensile results averaged across specimens tested in two mutually perpendicular orientations
direction.notes: No source-unstated orientation axes, weighting, direction-specific strength or universal isotropy are inferred.

evidence.locator: Article §§2.2–2.3, tensile method and vulcanized-sheet preparation/cutting: no separate post-preparation conditioning duration or environment for the tensile specimens is specified in these passages.

conditioning.notes: Tensile-specific pre-test conditioning time, temperature and humidity are not reported. Preparation, cure and density/foaming procedures are not substituted.

loading_rate.notes: Crosshead speed is not converted to a strain rate without source-reported gauge information.

fact.notes: Tensile-test relative humidity is not stated; no default humidity is assigned.

revised.scope_note: Study-qualified DCP-reactive PBS / 10 wt.% Indulin AT softwood kraft lignin formulation R10 (Ewurum and McDonald 2025); lignin percentage is relative to total polymer mass. The nominal DCP-containing formulation and source-reported reaction distinguish this R-series from the corresponding B-series simple blend. Table 1 reports a nonzero gel fraction of 4.7% for R10; this supports the source reaction distinction, not a certified final network or an extra selected property. Different lignin loadings distinguish the four candidates. Processing routes, specimens, translated labels and measured differences alone do not create additional identities. Composite denotes a lignin-filled polymer formulation, not a pure molecular species or a continuous-fiber laminate. The source says 0.25 wt.% DCP added to PBS. Its exact denominator and final retained DCP are not resolved; no final mass fractions, crosslink density, graft fraction, molecular architecture or chemical purity are inferred. Section 2.1 gives BioPBS FZ91PM/FZ91PB without resolving a single grade. Keep grade_id null; the R labels are study formulations, not commercial grades. One measured modulus per candidate; density, tensile strength, gel fraction and other properties are not appended. Catalog-only reference, not a universal constant or engineering allowable. Section 2.4 (PDF p.4) determines contextual gel fractions on hot-pressed DCP cross-linked PBS-lignin material, not the injection-molded tensile dog-bones. These results support formulation-level reaction context only and do not determine the tensile specimens’ gel fraction or final network.

The nominal DCP-containing formulation and source-reported reaction distinguish this R-series from the corresponding B-series simple blend. Table 1 reports a nonzero gel fraction of 4.7% for R10; this supports the source reaction distinction, not a certified final network or an extra selected property. Different lignin loadings distinguish the four candidates. Processing routes, specimens, translated labels and measured differences alone do not create additional identities. Composite denotes a lignin-filled polymer formulation, not a pure molecular species or a continuous-fiber laminate. The source says 0.25 wt.% DCP added to PBS. Its exact denominator and final retained DCP are not resolved; no final mass fractions, crosslink density, graft fraction, molecular architecture or chemical purity are inferred. Section 2.1 gives BioPBS FZ91PM/FZ91PB without resolving a single grade. Keep grade_id null; the R labels are study formulations, not commercial grades. Section 2.4 (PDF p.4) determines contextual gel fractions on hot-pressed DCP cross-linked PBS-lignin material, not the injection-molded tensile dog-bones. These results support formulation-level reaction context only and do not determine the tensile specimens’ gel fraction or final network.
